question_text: A Pb-Sn alloy contains $23 \%$ primary $\alpha$ and $77 \%$ eutectic microconstituent immediately after the eutectic reaction has been completed. Determine the composition of the alloy. Give your answer as the value of alloy_composition_percent_Sn.The unit of the answer is %.
response:
## Solution

For the Pb-Sn system, the relevant phase diagram values at the eutectic temperature (183°C) are:
- Eutectic composition: $C_E = 61.9$ wt% Sn
- Maximum solubility of Sn in α (Pb-rich solid): $C_\alpha = 18.3$ wt% Sn

The fraction of **primary α** is found using the lever rule applied just below the eutectic temperature, treating the primary α and the eutectic microconstituent as the two phases of the tie line between $C_\alpha$ and $C_E$:

$$f_{\text{primary }\alpha} = \frac{C_E - C_0}{C_E - C_\alpha}$$

Solving for the alloy composition $C_0$:

$$C_0 = C_E - f_{\text{primary }\alpha}\,(C_E - C_\alpha)$$

$$C_0 = 61.9 - 0.23\,(61.9 - 18.3) = 61.9 - 0.23 \times 43.6 = 61.9 - 10.028 = 51.872$$

$$\boxed{51.87}$$
